_notes: 10 pages. Early concept deck for the product branded 'Match Box' (later Tinder): a narrative problem story about a persona called Matt, four app mockups, a feature slide and a one-slide revenue model. Entirely pre-traction - not a single company number in the deck. No investor is named in the 10 slides and the deck states no date.

one_liner.value: The flirting game: like people around you and get connected if they like you too

expected_flags.note: no revenue figure; the 'Revenue Opportunity' slide describes an in-app purchase model only
no users, downloads, signups, launch date or any traction metric in 10 slides
no ask, round size, valuation or use of funds; the deck ends on the revenue model slide
no team slide; 'Matt' is a narrative persona in the problem story, and 'Matt Pouldar' appears only inside a mock chat screenshot - no founder is stated
no market sizing, no TAM/SAM and no named competitor in online dating
'$1 to see each new match' monetisation presented with no user, match-volume, conversion or ARPU assumption behind it
